_meta.indication: Treatment of anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) in adults who have been receiving dialysis for at least three months.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, active-controlled, non-inferiority, open-label trial; patients randomized 1:1 to VAFSEO (starting dose 300 mg once daily) or darbepoetin alfa.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with incident dialysis-dependent CKD who initiated dialysis within 16 weeks prior and were ESA-naive, had limited prior ESA use, or were maintained on ESAs.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in mean change of Hb from baseline to the primary evaluation period (Weeks 24 to 36).
pivotal_trials.result: Baseline-to-Week 24-36 Hb treatment difference (VAFSEO - darbepoetin alfa) -0.3 g/dL [95% CI -0.5, -0.1], meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.75 g/dL.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, active-controlled, non-inferiority, open-label trial; patients randomized 1:1 to VAFSEO (starting dose 300 mg once daily) or darbepoetin alfa.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults on chronic maintenance dialysis for more than 12 weeks who had converted from prior ESA therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference in mean change of Hb from baseline to the primary evaluation period (Weeks 24 to 36).
pivotal_trials.result: Baseline-to-Week 24-36 Hb treatment difference (VAFSEO - darbepoetin alfa) -0.2 g/dL [95% CI -0.2, -0.1], meeting the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.75 g/dL.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) included hypertension (14% vs 17% darbepoetin), diarrhea (13% vs 10%), headache (9% vs 8%), nausea (8% vs 8%) and fatigue (8% vs 5%). Serious risks include thrombotic vascular events (9.0 vs 8.7 per 100 PY), hepatotoxicity, hypertension, seizures, and gastrointestinal erosion.
target_moa: Vadadustat is a reversible inhibitor of HIF-prolyl-4-hydroxylases (PH1, PH2, PH3), stabilizing HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha transcription factors and increasing endogenous production of erythropoietin (EPO).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: INCREASED RISK OF DEATH, MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION, STROKE, VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM, AND THROMBOSIS OF VASCULAR ACCESS. VAFSEO increases the risk of thrombotic vascular events, including MACE; targeting a hemoglobin level greater than 11 g/dL is expected to further increase the risk of death and thrombotic events.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened; no issues were identified that would have benefitted from public discussion with external experts.

basis.text: The NDA resubmission was designated Priority review.

summary.text: VAFSEO was approved via a Priority-review NDA resubmission after the original NDA (received March 29, 2021) received a Complete Response Letter on March 29, 2022; the applicant narrowed to the dialysis-dependent CKD indication and addressed the CRL deficiencies. Approval was based on substantial evidence of effectiveness from two adequate and well-controlled non-inferiority trials (INNO2VATE-1 and INNO2VATE-2), with a required postmarketing observational safety study and a deferred pediatric study.

Akebia Therapeutics originally submitted their NDA for the treatment of anemia associated with CKD in adults on dialysis and not on dialysis on March 29, 2021. The Applicant received a CRL on March 29, 2022. The reasons for the CRL are briefly summarized below, see finalized CRL in DARRTS for further details.

The Applicant established substantial evidence of effectiveness for the proposed indication with two adequate and well-controlled trials, Study AKB-6548-CI-0016 (INNO2VATE 1) and Study AKB-6548-CI-0017 (INNO2VATE 2) that demonstrated non-inferiority of vadadustat to darbepoetin alfa (an approved erythropoietin stimulating agent (ESA)), based on hemoglobin (Hb) response in the DD-CKD populations.
